title: Vornoi Delaunay
comment: Vornoi Delaunay — The Delaunay triangulation is the dual of the Voronoi diagram. The most fundamental tool of computational geometry. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delaunay_triangulation
alt_text: Vornoi Delaunay. The Delaunay triangulation is the dual of the Voronoi diagram. The most fundamental tool of computational geometry.

title: Levelsets
comment: Levelsets — Classic reference: S. Osher and J. A. Sethian, Fronts propagating with curvature-dependent speed: Algorithms based on Hamilton-Jacobi formulations, 1988. Lays out the foundations of the level set method for curve and surface evolutions. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Level-set_method
alt_text: Levelsets. Classic reference: S. Osher and J. A. Sethian, Fronts propagating with curvature-dependent speed: Algorithms based on Hamilton-Jacobi formulations, 1988. Lays out the foundations of the level set method for curve and surface evolutions.

title: Dc Programming
comment: Dc Programming — Re-writing a non-convex optimization as a difference of convex (DC) leads to a simple iterative optimization method. Sometimes referred to as "convex-concave procedure" in the ML literature. http://www.lita.univ-lorraine.fr/~lethi/index.php/dca.html
alt_text: Dc Programming. Re-writing a non-convex optimization as a difference of convex (DC) leads to a simple iterative optimization method. Sometimes referred to as "convex-concave procedure" in the ML literature.

title: Kringing
comment: Kringing — Classic reference: D.G Krige, A statistical approach to some mine valuations and allied problems at the Witwatersrand, 1951. Kriging (also known as Wiener interpolation) accounts for uncertainty in kernel interpolation using a Gaussian processes. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kriging
alt_text: Kringing. Classic reference: D.G Krige, A statistical approach to some mine valuations and allied problems at the Witwatersrand, 1951. Kriging (also known as Wiener interpolation) accounts for uncertainty in kernel interpolation using a Gaussian processes.

title: Tutte
comment: Tutte — Tutte embedding is the solution of a Poisson equation. Iterative resolution is equivalent to a system of masses and springs. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tutte_embedding
alt_text: Tutte. Tutte embedding is the solution of a Poisson equation. Iterative resolution is equivalent to a system of masses and springs.

title: Cox
comment: Cox — Classic reference: Maurice G. Cox, The Numerical Evaluation of B-Splines, 1972. Introduced (with De Boor) an efficient algorithm for the evaluation of B-splines, which revolutionized CAGD. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_Boor%27s_algorithm
alt_text: Cox. Classic reference: Maurice G. Cox, The Numerical Evaluation of B-Splines, 1972. Introduced (with De Boor) an efficient algorithm for the evaluation of B-splines, which revolutionized CAGD.

title: Dykstra Pocs
comment: Dykstra Pocs — POCS, Dykstra and DR often succeed in finding points in the intersection of possibly non-convex sets. Dykstra and DR usually work better. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Projections_onto_convex_sets
alt_text: Dykstra Pocs. POCS, Dykstra and DR often succeed in finding points in the intersection of possibly non-convex sets. Dykstra and DR usually work better.

title: Multipoles
comment: Multipoles — Classic reference: L. Greengard and V. Rokhlin, A Fast Algorithm for Particle Simulations, 1987. Evaluates in O(n) in place of O(n^2) sums involving long-range interaction kernels. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast_multipole_method
alt_text: Multipoles. Classic reference: L. Greengard and V. Rokhlin, A Fast Algorithm for Particle Simulations, 1987. Evaluates in O(n) in place of O(n^2) sums involving long-range interaction kernels.

title: Maxcut
comment: Maxcut — MAX-CUT is an NP hard problem. Goemans and Williamson SDP relaxation with randomized thresholding achieves a 0.879-approximation. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maximum_cut
alt_text: Maxcut. MAX-CUT is an NP hard problem. Goemans and Williamson SDP relaxation with randomized thresholding achieves a 0.879-approximation.

title: Optical Flow
comment: Optical Flow — Classic reference: B.K.P. Horn and B.G. Schunck, Determining optical flow, 1981. Computes optical flow by a quadratic regularization of the brightness constancy constraint. Solution is obtained by solving a linear system. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horn%E2%80%93Schunck_method
alt_text: Optical Flow. Classic reference: B.K.P. Horn and B.G. Schunck, Determining optical flow, 1981. Computes optical flow by a quadratic regularization of the brightness constancy constraint. Solution is obtained by solving a linear system.

title: Bernoulli
comment: Bernoulli — The Brachistochrone problem was solved by Bernoulli and is the birth of calculus of variations. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calculus_of_variations
alt_text: Bernoulli. The Brachistochrone problem was solved by Bernoulli and is the birth of calculus of variations.

title: Chan Vese
comment: Chan Vese — Classic reference: T F. Chan, L. A. Vese, Active Contours Without Edges, 2001. The simplest yet most celebrated region-based segmentation method. Minimizes a binary Mumford-Shah segmentation functional using the level set method. https://www.ipol.im/pub/art/2012/g-cv/
alt_text: Chan Vese. Classic reference: T F. Chan, L. A. Vese, Active Contours Without Edges, 2001. The simplest yet most celebrated region-based segmentation method. Minimizes a binary Mumford-Shah segmentation functional using the level set method.

title: Smacoff
comment: Smacoff — SMACOF is the most popular stress minimization algorithm for multidimensional scaling (for dimensionality reduction or shape flattening). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stress_majorization
alt_text: Smacoff. SMACOF is the most popular stress minimization algorithm for multidimensional scaling (for dimensionality reduction or shape flattening).

title: Planar Graphs
comment: Planar Graphs — Classic reference: K Wagner, Bemerkungen zum Vierfarbenproblem, 1936. Later improved by Komuro. Any pair of planar triangulations of n vertices can be connected by O(n) edge flips (despite the exponential number of such triangulations). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flip_graph
alt_text: Planar Graphs. Classic reference: K Wagner, Bemerkungen zum Vierfarbenproblem, 1936. Later improved by Komuro. Any pair of planar triangulations of n vertices can be connected by O(n) edge flips (despite the exponential number of such triangulations).

title: Min Max
comment: Min Max — Min/max games are convex/concave saddle points. Can be solved by primal-dual algorithms. Converges to Dirac mass strategies only when K has a single saddle point, otherwise selects mixed strategies. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minimax
alt_text: Min Max. Min/max games are convex/concave saddle points. Can be solved by primal-dual algorithms. Converges to Dirac mass strategies only when K has a single saddle point, otherwise selects mixed strategies.

title: Inpainting
comment: Inpainting — Classic reference: JA. Criminisi; P. Perez; K. Toyama, Region filling and object removal by exemplar-based image inpainting, 2004. Introduces the idea of doing inpainting by pixel recopy. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inpainting
alt_text: Inpainting. Classic reference: JA. Criminisi; P. Perez; K. Toyama, Region filling and object removal by exemplar-based image inpainting, 2004. Introduces the idea of doing inpainting by pixel recopy.

title: Edge Collapse
comment: Edge Collapse — Edge collapse is a fundamental mesh processing primitive, at the heart of many mesh simplification methods. Influential papers by Hoppe, Garland and Heckbert. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progressive_meshes
alt_text: Edge Collapse. Edge collapse is a fundamental mesh processing primitive, at the heart of many mesh simplification methods. Influential papers by Hoppe, Garland and Heckbert.

title: Stft
comment: Stft — Classic reference: J Allen, Short Time Spectral Analysis, Synthesis, and Modification by Discrete Fourier Transform, 1977. Popularized the use of the spectrogram as the baseline tool for audio processing. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spectrogram
alt_text: Stft. Classic reference: J Allen, Short Time Spectral Analysis, Synthesis, and Modification by Discrete Fourier Transform, 1977. Popularized the use of the spectrogram as the baseline tool for audio processing.

title: Grad Flow
comment: Grad Flow — The gradient field defines the steepest descent direction. The gradient flow dynamic defines a segmentation of the space into attraction basins of the local minimizers. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gradient
alt_text: Grad Flow. The gradient field defines the steepest descent direction. The gradient flow dynamic defines a segmentation of the space into attraction basins of the local minimizers.
